title: At 12 months, babble matched English or Spanish prosody only after exposure to both
summary: Sundara and colleagues found that 12-month-olds matched babbling prosody to English or Spanish only if they had some exposure to both.
body: Megha Sundara, Nancy Ward, Barbara Conboy, and Patricia Kuhl compared 12-month-olds talking with people who spoke Spanish and English. Monolingual English-learning infants who had about 5 hours of Spanish, and infants learning both languages, matched the prosody of their babbling to the language of the person they were with. Monolingual English-learning infants with no Spanish exposure did not. The result is about melody and rhythm of babble in this laboratory comparison. It is not a ranking of one language over another, and it is not a vocabulary-size result.

sources.title: Exposure to a second language in infancy alters speech production
sources.author: Megha Sundara, Nancy Ward, Barbara Conboy, and Patricia K. Kuhl
sources.note: Opened 2026-11-26 at the PMC page. Supports the abstract's three-group result on matching babbling prosody at 12 months.
